headline: Oil prices climb back toward $100, and the record-breaking rally for US stocks stalls
summary: Oil prices rose after the latest threats to the U.S.-Iran ceasefire, while U.S. stocks stalled near record highs. The S&P 500 slipped 0.3% on Wednesday from its all-time high.
why: Crude oil prices feed into inflation, energy costs and corporate margins, and Middle East tensions are a major driver of supply risk. The S&P 500 is the benchmark index for large US companies.

impacts.name: S&P 500
impacts.why: The index slipped 0.3% from its all-time high on Wednesday as stocks stalled.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Oil prices rose after renewed threats to the U.S.-Iran ceasefire, which lifted energy-price concerns and weighed on equities that had been near record highs.
